items.stem: Give any three reasons why statistics is important in economics.
items.answer: Presents facts precisely; condenses mass data into summary measures; helps find relationships (e.g. between price and demand); helps in policy formulation and forecasting.

items.stem:
Pooja, a Class 11 student in Patna, wants to study how families in her locality spend their income. She plans to ask 60 families about their monthly income, the number of members, the type of house and their religion, and then present the data in tables and graphs.
(i) Which of these characteristics are quantitative and which are qualitative? (ii) Name the stages of the statistical study she will follow. (iii) State one limitation of the results she will get.
items.answer: (i) Quantitative: monthly income, number of members; qualitative: type of house, religion (ii) collection → organisation → presentation → analysis → interpretation (iii) results describe the group on average, not each family; qualitative aspects are only counted.
items.markingKey: (i) 2 marks; (ii) 1 mark; (iii) 1 mark.

items.stem: Explain the meaning of statistics in the singular and plural sense with an example of each.

items.markingKey: 2 marks: meaning/scope; 3 marks: importance with examples; 1 mark: conclusion (6 marks).
